title: Shallow Safety Alignment on Phi-3-Mini: Do Smaller Models Show the Same First-Token Shortcut?

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if shallow alignment is more pronounced in small models, on-device LLM deployments carry higher risk. Directly relevant to deployment safety decisions.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Replication study: measure refusal prefix concentration and test prefilling on one model. No training, just inference. Accessible for beginners with medium compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped replication: measure refusal prefix rate, test prefilling attack, plot alignment depth curve. One model, one well-defined protocol from the original paper.

novelty.reasoning: The shallow alignment phenomenon is well-established for 7B+ models, but no published work has specifically tested whether Phi-3-Mini or other sub-4B models exhibit more or less pronounced shallow alignment. The Phi-3 safety paper focuses on training methodology, not alignment depth. This replication on a smaller model fills a genuine gap.

evidence.source: Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep (Qi et al., ICLR 2025)
evidence.finding: Establishes the shallow alignment phenomenon on Llama-2-7B-Chat (96.1% refusal prefix concentration) and larger models, but does not test sub-4B models like Phi-3-Mini.
Describes Phi-3 safety alignment methodology but does not measure alignment depth or test for shallow alignment vulnerability.

evidence.source: EASE: Efficient Safety Alignment for Small Language Models (arXiv 2511.06512, 2025)
evidence.finding: Proposes efficient safety alignment methods for small LMs but does not specifically characterize whether shallow alignment is more pronounced in smaller models.
